chapter: Television, vocal albums and orchestral craft
title: Joe Maini
summary: Mandel calls Joe Maini the best lead alto he knew, a funny, Parker-influenced player who feigned ignorance but was intelligent.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Now one of the key players on, I Want to Live! and you mentioned he played lead alto on the Sinatra record was Joe Maini.
Let’s talk a bit about him.

He was one the most amazing alto players I’ve ever known and do I miss him, we lost him in the early 60s and he’s the best lead alto player I know. All you have to do is listen to all the Terry Gibbs, Dream Band records. He was a wonderful soloist and he had great emotional appeal, he was not of the cool school and I'm not one who liked the cool school, particularly.
He was a very Charlie Parker influenced alto player.

And he was one of the funniest people I've ever known and unknown to most people he was very literate. He was a professional ignoramus who pretended to be, it was an act with him, he was extremely intelligent.
